title: Data-Driven Assessment of Wind Energy Potential in Borneo, Malaysia: Implications for Sustainable Renewable Energy Development
content: Realistic view on potential wind energy harvesting in Borneo Sarawak is necessary and promising data should be gathered to support a government in green energy landscape. Recent research normally gathered a data from a height of less than 30 m, and it does not align with the model wind turbine that normally build with height more than 30 m. Mukah Sarawak is selected as a matter of fact significantly higher wind speed data from Meteorological Department (MET) Malaysia as compared to 6 others location. An accurate of 96.38% low-cost monitoring system has been applied at proposed location, and the data is gathered from October 2024 to March 2025 considering a potential stronger wind speed due to northeast monsoon. Beta distribution with α = 2.5; β = 6.8 is used for modeling wind speed frequency. As compared to others Normal, F, Gamma and Weibull distributions, MSE results of 0.66% for Beta distribution are the lowest. The trend indicates left skewed distribution, with lower wind speed occurring more frequently between 1.5 m/s to 4.0 m/s. The wind seems to gradually decrease after 4 m/s, showing stronger wind occur less frequently. Supporting peak wind hours (PWH) graph shows a potential wind speed of 2 hours but indicates lack of consistency and less predictable wind speed, therefore conclude Mukah is unsuited for harvesting wind energy. Future study should be expended to offshore areas that promise a stronger wind speed but challenge in marine environment should be considered for a profitable wind power station.
